title: Respiration

final_note: You worked through Respiration — 23 specification statements.

concepts.def: An exothermic reaction which is continuously occurring in living cells, transferring energy from glucose. The energy transferred supplies all the energy needed for living processes.
A reaction that transfers energy to the surroundings. Because respiration is exothermic, respiring cells and tissues get warmer as energy is transferred.

concepts.term: Uses of the energy transferred by respiration
concepts.def: Organisms need energy for chemical reactions to build larger molecules, for movement, and for keeping warm. The energy transferred is also used for the continual enzyme controlled processes of metabolism that synthesise new molecules.
Respiration in cells that takes place using oxygen. Glucose is completely oxidised, so a relatively large amount of energy is transferred compared with anaerobic respiration.
Respiration in cells that takes place without oxygen, to transfer energy. The products differ from those of aerobic respiration and much less energy is transferred.
Aerobic respiration is represented by the equation: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.
C6H12O6 is glucose, O2 is oxygen, CO2 is carbon dioxide and H2O is water. These symbols are used in place of the words in the equation for aerobic respiration.
Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by the equation: glucose → lactic acid. No carbon dioxide or water is produced by this reaction.
In anaerobic respiration the oxidation of glucose is incomplete, so much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

concepts.term: Anaerobic respiration in plant and yeast cells
concepts.def: Anaerobic respiration in plant and yeast cells is represented by the equation: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide.

Anaerobic respiration in yeast cells. It has economic importance in the manufacture of bread, where the carbon dioxide makes the dough rise, and of alcoholic drinks, which contain the ethanol produced.

concepts.term: Response of the body to exercise
concepts.def: During exercise the human body reacts to the increased demand for energy. The heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume increase during exercise to supply the muscles with more oxygenated blood.

concepts.term: Muscle fatigue and oxygen debt in exercise
concepts.def: If insufficient oxygen is supplied, anaerobic respiration takes place in muscles. The incomplete oxidation of glucose causes a build up of lactic acid and creates an oxygen debt. During long periods of vigorous activity muscles become fatigued and stop contracting efficiently.

concepts.term: Oxygen debt and the fate of lactic acid
concepts.def: Blood flowing through the muscles transports the lactic acid to the liver, where it is converted back into glucose. Oxygen debt is the amount of extra oxygen the body needs after exercise to react with the accumulated lactic acid and remove it from the cells.

The sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body. The energy transferred by respiration in cells is used by the organism for these continual enzyme controlled processes, which synthesise new molecules.

Metabolism includes: conversion of glucose to starch, glycogen and cellulose; the formation of lipid molecules from a molecule of glycerol and three molecules of fatty acids; the use of glucose and nitrate ions to form amino acids which in turn are used to synthesise proteins; respiration; and the breakdown of excess proteins to form urea for excretion.

concepts.term: Small molecules used in synthesis and breakdown
concepts.def: Sugars are used to synthesise carbohydrates such as starch, glycogen and cellulose; amino acids are used to synthesise proteins, and excess protein is broken down to form urea; glycerol and fatty acids are used to synthesise lipids. Breakdown of these larger molecules releases the same small molecules again.

options: an endothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening during hard exercise
an exothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening when we breathe in
mcqs.explain: Cellular respiration is an exothermic reaction which is continuously occurring in living cells, transferring the energy needed for living processes.

mcqs.q: How does anaerobic respiration in muscle cells compare with aerobic respiration?
options: far more energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and ethanol made as well
less energy transferred, and carbon dioxide made
mcqs.explain: Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by glucose → lactic acid, and because the oxidation of glucose is incomplete much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of the energy transferred by respiration?
options: creating new energy inside the living cell
moving oxygen from the lungs to the blood
building larger molecules from smaller ones
breaking large molecules into smaller ones
mcqs.explain: Organisms need energy for chemical reactions to build larger molecules, as well as for movement and keeping warm.

mcqs.q: Which word equation represents aerobic respiration?
options: glucose + oxygen → lactic acid + water
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen → ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
mcqs.explain: This is the equation given in the specification for aerobic respiration: glucose and oxygen are used and carbon dioxide and water are produced.

mcqs.q: In the equation for aerobic respiration, what do the symbols C6H12O6 and H2O represent?
options: C6H12O6 is glucose and H2O is oxygen
C6H12O6 is oxygen gas and H2O is water
C6H12O6 is water and H2O is glucose
C6H12O6 is glucose and H2O is water
mcqs.explain: C6H12O6 is the symbol for glucose, the reactant, and H2O is the symbol for water, one of the products.

mcqs.q: A muscle cell has no oxygen supply. Which substance builds up in the cell?
options: liquid ethanol, made from glucose
lactic acid, made from glucose
water vapour, made from glucose
carbon dioxide, made from glucose
mcqs.explain: Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by the equation glucose → lactic acid, so lactic acid builds up when insufficient oxygen is supplied.

mcqs.q: Why is much less energy transferred by anaerobic respiration than by aerobic respiration?
options: the oxidation of the glucose is faster
the glucose in cells is used up faster
the energy is used up making lactic acid
the oxidation of the glucose is incomplete
mcqs.explain: As the oxidation of glucose is incomplete in anaerobic respiration, much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

mcqs.q: Yeast is used in the manufacture of bread and alcoholic drinks. Which equation represents the respiration of the yeast in these processes?
options: glucose → lactic acid + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen → ethanol + water
glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose + water → ethanol + oxygen
mcqs.explain: Anaerobic respiration in plant and yeast cells is represented by this equation. In yeast it is called fermentation: the carbon dioxide makes bread rise and the ethanol is in alcoholic drinks.

mcqs.q: How does the body react to the increased demand for energy during exercise?
options: the heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume rise
the breathing rate rises but the heart rate stays steady
the heart rate rises but the breath volume is steady
the breath volume rises but the heart rate is steady
mcqs.explain: The heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume increase during exercise to supply the muscles with more oxygenated blood.

mcqs.q: A sprinter's muscles are not supplied with enough oxygen during a race. What happens in the muscles?
options: lactic acid builds up and an oxygen debt forms
carbon dioxide builds up and an oxygen debt forms
ethanol builds up and an oxygen debt is formed
lactic acid builds up and more energy is made
mcqs.explain: If insufficient oxygen is supplied, anaerobic respiration takes place in muscles; the incomplete oxidation of glucose causes a build up of lactic acid and creates an oxygen debt.

mcqs.q: After a race, what happens to the lactic acid that has built up in the muscles?
options: it is taken in the blood to the liver
it is broken down inside the muscles
it is breathed out through the lungs
it is turned to glucose in the blood
mcqs.explain: Blood flowing through the muscles transports the lactic acid to the liver where it is converted back into glucose.

mcqs.q: How is a lipid molecule formed in metabolism?
options: from three glycerols and one fatty acid
from a single glycerol and three amino acids
from three fatty acids and one glucose
from one glycerol and three fatty acids
mcqs.explain: Metabolism includes the formation of lipid molecules from a molecule of glycerol and three molecules of fatty acids.

mcqs.q: A plant cell synthesises protein. Which molecules does its metabolism use?
options: glucose and fatty acids, to make amino acids
glucose and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
glycerol and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
starch and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
mcqs.explain: Metabolism includes the use of glucose and nitrate ions to form amino acids which in turn are used to synthesise proteins.
